prompt:
Below is a plan for a software change. Decide, for each reference problem, whether the plan addresses the same underlying problem anywhere in its text (names it as a risk, or plans for it specifically), even if worded differently.

Change request: Make ky retry POST and PATCH requests by default when the network fails, so that flaky mobile connections stop failing.

Reference problems:
1. Adding post and patch to defaultRetryOptions.methods in source/utils/normalize.ts would cause Ky to retry on retry.statusCodes (such as 500, 502, 503, and 504) as well as network failures, violating the request to only retry when the network fails. This would re-execute failed server-side mutations for HTTP error responses that should have failed immediately.
2. Because POST and PATCH are non-idempotent methods, retrying on a NetworkError introduces duplicate server-side side effects if the connection was interrupted after the server received and processed the initial mutation. Ky has no way of discerning whether a network failure occurred before the request reached the server or after the server began handling it.
3. In source/core/Ky.ts, connection drops produce a NetworkError whereas request timeouts throw a TimeoutError, which is governed separately by retry.retryOnTimeout (defaulting to false). Flaky mobile connections frequently fail via timeouts, meaning the change would either fail to resolve mobile drops or, if retryOnTimeout is broadened, unsafely retry requests that the server is still actively executing.
4. In source/core/Ky.ts, #fetch() calls this.request.clone() whenever retry.limit > 0, which invokes ReadableStream#tee() on streaming bodies. Enabling retries for POST and PATCH by default will force every streaming upload to buffer unconsumed chunks in memory, risking excessive memory consumption or out-of-memory crashes on resource-constrained mobile devices.
5. If a POST or PATCH request body is a ReadableStream that was disturbed or locked during an interrupted initial attempt, Request.clone() in #fetch() will throw an unhandled TypeError on the retry attempt rather than recovering cleanly. This would cause flaky mobile requests to crash with native stream errors rather than surfacing a clean NetworkError.
6. When using onUploadProgress, streamRequest in source/utils/body.ts pipes the request body through a progress-tracking transform stream. Retrying an interrupted POST or PATCH upload will cause progress events to restart from 0%, triggering confusing progress regressions or duplicate completion events in client UIs.
7. Existing custom retry.shouldRetry hooks that return undefined rely on Ky falling through to default method checks that reject POST and PATCH. Enabling POST and PATCH retries by default would alter this fallback behavior, silently triggering retries for existing applications that expect undefined to reject non-idempotent requests.
8. This change directly breaks existing test assertions in test/retry.ts—specifically tests like 'not on POST' and 'NetworkError is not retried for non-retriable method (POST)'—which enforce that POST requests fail fast without retrying. Changing this default represents a breaking change in Ky's core HTTP semantics for existing consumers.
9. POST and PATCH mutations frequently carry headers such as Idempotency-Key or authorization nonces generated for a single attempt. Retrying automatically without re-running beforeRequest hooks or providing a mechanism to refresh request-specific tokens will cause backends to reject retried requests as duplicate or invalid submissions.
10. Compatibility with existing retry config – Projects may already specify a custom retry object that omits methods. Overriding the default could unintentionally extend the retry set, breaking assumptions in tests or CI pipelines.
11. Network‑error detection – Ky decides whether an error is “network” via isNetworkError. Certain mobile edge cases (e.g., DNS‑lookup failures) may be classified differently, causing inconsistent retry behavior for POST/PATCH versus GET.
12. Server‑side rate limiting – Automatic retries on POST/PATCH may repeatedly hit rate‑limit responses (429) and ignore afterStatusCodes handling, leading to rapid back‑off loops and possible bans.

Plan:
I stopped at [term] as asked. No project files were edited; the plan is in `~/…/claude-home/plans/standard-make-ky-retry-agile-toast.md`. One independent [term] round returned REVISE with 10 findings. I checked them against the code, and the plan now addresses all of them. A second [term] round has not been run.

**Assumptions (no questions asked):**
- "When the network fails" means a `NetworkError` only. It does not include HTTP 5xx/408/429 responses or timeouts.
- This changes default behaviour of a published library, so it is a semver-major change. Releasing it is out of scope.
- ky will not add an `Idempotency-Key` header itself, because a custom header triggers a CORS preflight. The readme gets a recipe instead.
- The repo has no lessons file; `AGENTS.md`'s rule against `null` applies.
- The prior art on how other HTTP clients handle this came from memory. I did not verify it online in this run.

**Key finding:** the obvious one-line change is to add `'post','patch'` to the default `retry.methods` (`source/utils/normalize.ts:17`). That is wrong. In `#calculateRetryDelay` (`source/core/Ky.ts:703`), the method check comes before any error-type check. So that change would also retry POSTs on 500, 502, 503, 504, 408 and 429, which often arrive after the server has already written the data.

**Chosen design:** a new option, `retry.networkErrorMethods`, defaulting to `['post', 'patch']`.
- A method that is in this list but not in `methods` is retried only on a `NetworkError`.
- `shouldRetry` can veto that retry by returning `false`. Returning `true` cannot turn an HTTP error on a POST into a retry.
- Timeouts on these methods are not retried, even with `retryOnTimeout: true`.
- `ky.retry()` from a hook works as before.
- Setting the option to `null` or a non-array throws a `TypeError` that names the option.

**What the [term] caught:**
- ky concatenates nested arrays when merging options. So a request-level `networkErrorMethods: []` does not cancel an instance-level `['post']`. The working opt-outs are `replaceOption([])` or `retry: 0`.
- An existing test, "NetworkError is not retried for non-retriable method (POST)" (`test/retry.ts:3766`), contradicts the new default and has to be converted.
- Users who set `methods: ['get']` currently get "only GET retries". After the change, POST and PATCH would still retry on network errors.
- In Chromium, streaming uploads over HTTP/1.1 always fail with a network error. Every POST with `onUploadProgress` would use up its retries on an upload that cannot succeed.

**Deliverables:**
- **D01:** types and validation for the new option
- **D02:** the retry decision change in `Ky.ts`
- **D03:** test updates, including a check that the new tests fail when the change is reverted
- **D04:** readme and doc-comment updates
- **D05:** a breaking-change note

**This may not meet the stated goal.** The default timing gives about 1 s of retries (2 retries, 300 ms then 600 ms). Mobile dropouts often last longer, so the plan documents `limit`, `delay` and `backoffLimit` rather than changing them.

| # | Risk | Why it bites here | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Duplicate writes (double order or payment) | "Failed to fetch" and Undici's `terminated` also fire when the server committed the write and only the response was lost; browsers can't tell the two apart | Prominent warning, `Idempotency-Key` recipe, release as a major version |
| 2 | POST retried on 5xx | The method check runs before the error-type check (`Ky.ts:703`) | Separate option limited to `NetworkError`; tests that 500/503/408/429 are not retried |
| 3 | Opt-out silently doesn't work | Nested arrays are concatenated on merge (`merge.ts:441`) | Document `replaceOption([])` or `retry: 0`; test both |
| 4 | Silent change for `methods: ['get']` users | That setting used to mean "only GET retries" | Breaking-change note and readme text |
| 5 | `shouldRetry` contract changes | Its docs and a test say it is never called for POST | Call it only for network errors; `true` can't turn an HTTP error into a retry |
| 6 | Uploads that can't succeed use up all retries | Chromium streaming uploads over HTTP/1.1 always fail with a network error | Document the `beforeRetry` workaround; add a test |
| 7 | Tests changed just to pass | Existing tests assume POST is never retried (`test/retry.ts:322`, `:3766`) | Convert them, keep default-POST counterparts, check the new tests fail when the change is reverted |
| 8 | `null` handled inconsistently | `AGENTS.md` bans `null`; sibling array options throw a plain `Error` | Throw a `TypeError` that names `retry.networkErrorMethods` |
| 9 | Goal not met | About 1 s of default backoff is shorter than most mobile outages | Document `limit`, `delay`, `backoffLimit` |
| 10 | Hidden effect on `Request` objects and hooks | The check reads `this.request.method`; retry options are re-read on every decision | Tests for a `Request` input with a stream body and for a hook changing the option |

Riskiest: #1. Retrying a POST whose write already happened duplicates side effects, and no client-side check can prevent that without server-side idempotency keys.
